key_terms.meaning: An expression that evaluates to exactly True or False, e.g. marks >= 40 or (a > b) and (b > 0).
A chain that tests conditions top to bottom and runs only the first block whose condition is True; else runs when none match.
Repeats its indented block as long as the tested condition stays True; the condition is re-checked before every pass.
Repeats its block once for each item of an iterable, binding the loop variable to the current item.
range(start, stop, step) produces the integers start, start+step, ... up to but not including stop.
A variable set before the loop (e.g. total = 0) and updated inside it (total = total + x) to build a running result.
A loop written inside another loop; the inner loop completes all its iterations for every single iteration of the outer loop.
Leaves the innermost enclosing loop immediately; control jumps to the first statement after the loop.
Skips the remaining statements of the current iteration and moves to the next iteration of the same loop.
A statement that does nothing; used where Python's syntax requires a statement but no action is needed.
A named block of statements defined once with def and executed whenever its name is called.
The value a function sends back with return; a function that ends without return gives back None.
A formal parameter is the name in the def line; an actual argument is the value supplied at the call.
A parameter given a value in the def line, used when the call omits that argument; it must follow all non-default parameters.
An argument passed as name=value at the call, matching the parameter by name instead of by position.
The region, namely one function call, in which a name assigned inside a function can be seen; outside it NameError occurs.
The period during which the object a variable refers to stays alive, that is, while at least one reference to it exists.
A technique where a function calls itself on a smaller version of the same problem.
The condition in a recursive function that returns without calling itself, so the chain of calls stops.
lambda parameters: expression builds a small anonymous function whose body is a single expression that is returned.

takeaways: A conditional chain runs exactly one branch: the first one whose condition is True, or else the else block.
Indentation, not braces, decides which statements belong to an if or a loop body in Python.
A while loop suits an unknown number of repeats; a for loop suits walking through a known iterable.
break, continue and pass change loop behaviour without changing the loop condition.
A function hides repeated steps behind a name, so the same logic is written once and called many times.
Python matches actual arguments to formal parameters by position first, then by keyword, then by default value.
Local names live inside one call and disappear afterwards; global names live for the whole program run.
Every correct recursive function needs a base case and progress towards it, otherwise the call stack overflows.
lambda with map, filter and reduce replaces short throwaway loops with one-line expressions.
bank_note: Long answers usually ask for a working program plus explanation, so keep the code correct, show sample input and output, and state each term's definition before using it.

bank.q: Explain the if-elif-else chain with a program that prints a student's grade from marks. Why does Python test the conditions in order and stop at the first True one?
outline: Syntax of if, elif, else with correct indentation
Grade boundaries written as boolean expressions tested top to bottom
Only one block runs; else acts as the catch-all
Sample input 72 gives grade B, showing one branch only
Mention that a wrong order (lowest boundary first) gives wrong results

bank.q: Compare the while loop and the for loop in Python. State two situations where each is the better choice and give a short program for each.
outline: while: condition tested before each pass, count must be managed by the programmer
for: iterates over an iterable such as range, string or list
Risk of an infinite while loop when the counter is never updated
for is safer when the number of items is known
One correct small program each, with output

bank.q: Define an accumulator. Write a program using a for loop that reads 10 numbers and prints their sum and average, and mark the accumulator variable.
outline: Accumulator initialised before the loop (total = 0)
Updated inside the loop (total = total + n)
Average = total / count, count tracked separately if needed
Correct indentation and a for loop over range(10)

bank.q: Explain break, continue and pass with one small program each. How does break inside a nested loop behave?
outline: break leaves the innermost loop only
continue returns to the loop test, skipping the rest of the body
pass is a no-op placeholder, useful in an empty block or a stub function
Nested example: inner break exits the inner loop, outer loop continues
Correct output shown for each snippet

bank.q: Write a function is_prime(n) that returns True or False, and use it to print all primes below 50. Explain the parameter, the local variable and the return value.
outline: def line with one formal parameter n
Early return False for n < 2
Loop up to int(n**0.5) with a divisor test
Boolean True returned at the end
Caller loop over range(2, 50) using the returned value
Identification of parameter, local names, return value

bank.q: Write a function that takes a list of marks and returns the highest, lowest and average using a single pass. Then use a nested loop to print a pattern of stars, and explain both codes.
outline: One function, one loop, three accumulators
Tuple returned and unpacked by the caller
Nested loop: outer loop controls rows, inner loop controls columns
Star pattern output shown exactly
Note that the inner loop restarts for each outer iteration

bank.q: Write a function with default and keyword arguments, for example def bill(amount, tax=0.05, discount=0), and show three different legal calls plus one illegal call. Explain the matching rules.
outline: Positional matching from the left
Keyword matching by parameter name, order free
Default used when the argument is missing
Illegal call: non-default after default, or unexpected keyword name
Sample outputs such as bill(1000, discount=100)

bank.q: Write a recursive function to compute the sum of digits of a number and another to compute n!. Trace the calls for n = 4 and state the base case of each.
outline: Base case: single digit for digit sum; n == 0 or 1 for factorial
Recursive case with a strictly smaller argument
Call trace showing the stack building and unwinding
Final answers: digit sum of 4729 is 22, 4! is 24
Consequence of a missing base case: RecursionError

bank.q: Using lambda with map, filter and reduce, write one expression each to square a list, keep only the even numbers, and find the product of a list. Show the imports needed.
outline: from functools import reduce for reduce
list(map(lambda x: x*x, nums))
list(filter(lambda x: x % 2 == 0, nums))
reduce(lambda a, b: a*b, nums)
Note that map and filter return lazy iterators in Python 3, so wrap in list to display

bank.q: A student writes a loop that never ends and a program that raises UnboundLocalError inside a function. Analyse both faults using the concepts of loop condition and variable scope, and give corrected code.
outline: Infinite loop: the variable used in the condition is never updated, or the update is outside the body
Fix: update the counter inside the loop, or use a for loop over a range
UnboundLocalError: assignment inside the function makes the name local for the whole call, so reading it first fails
Fixes: pass the value as a parameter, return it, or declare global (with the warning against relying on global)
Corrected snippets for both

bank.q: Compare a recursive solution and an iterative solution for the nth Fibonacci number. Discuss time cost, memory on the call stack, readability and the danger of deep recursion. Which would you choose for n = 40?
outline: Naive recursion repeats work: roughly exponential time
Iterative version keeps two variables and runs in linear time with constant memory
Recursion uses one stack frame per pending call; Python's default recursion limit is about 1000
RecursionError risk for large n, and the same limit applies to other deep calls
Verdict: iterative for large n, recursion for clarity when depth is small
Possible mention of memoisation as a middle path

bank.q: Explain scope and lifetime with a program containing a global variable, a local variable of the same name, and a function that modifies the global. Predict the output line by line and justify it.
outline: Name lookup order: local, enclosing, global, built-in
A local name shadows the global name inside the function
global statement needed to rebind the global from inside a function
Lifetime of the global object lasts until the program ends; the local object may be freed after the call
Exact output predicted for each print

bank.q: Design a menu-driven program using functions for a small UPI-style wallet: deposit, withdraw and show balance, with input validation and an exit option. Explain how functions, loops, conditionals, break and default arguments fit together.
outline: One function per operation with a clear name and parameters
Balance kept in one place and returned or passed, not duplicated as scattered globals
while True menu loop with break on exit
if-elif-else for menu choice, continue for invalid input
Default argument such as a minimum withdrawal amount
Input validation and a clean final output

bank.q: Why does Python treat functions as first-class objects, and how does that make lambda with map, filter and reduce useful? Illustrate with a list of prices in rupees and a 10 percent discount.
outline: A function can be stored in a variable, passed and returned
map applies a function to each item, filter keeps items where it is True, reduce folds to one value
Example: list(map(lambda p: p*0.9, prices)) and filter with a price limit
Readability trade-off: lambda is fine for one short expression, a def is clearer for longer logic
Note lazy iterators in Python 3

glossary.def: A boolean expression whose True or False value decides which block runs.
Short for else-if; adds another condition to test when the earlier ones were False.
The optional final block of an if chain, run when no condition matched.
Leading spaces at the start of a line that group statements into a block in Python.
Any object that yields its items one at a time in a for loop, such as a string, list, tuple or range.
The name in a for statement that is bound to the current item on each pass.
A loop whose condition never becomes False, so it runs until the program is stopped or a break runs.
A special input value that signals the end of data and is often paired with a while loop and break.
The indented statements that are repeated on every iteration.
One complete pass through the statements of a loop body.
Writing the function name followed by parentheses, with arguments inside, to run the body.
The def statement that creates a function object and binds it to a name.
A value supplied at a function call.
A name listed in the def line that receives an argument when the function is called.
An argument matched to a parameter by its order in the call.
Python's value for 'nothing here'; it is what a function returns when no return statement runs.
A function that performs an action but returns None.
A name created at module level and visible throughout the file.
A declaration inside a function saying that a name refers to the module-level variable, allowing rebinding.
The record of function calls still in progress, each with its own local namespace.
The part of a recursive function that calls itself with a smaller or simpler argument.
A function that takes another function as an argument or returns one, as map and filter do.
A function with no name bound to it, typically created with lambda.
